Jimmy Butler was born on September 14, 1989.
Jimmy Butler is an American professional basketball player.
Jimmy Butler plays for the Miami Heat of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
Nicknames given to Jimmy Butler include "Jimmy Buckets".
Jimmy Butler has been a six-time NBA All-Star.
Jimmy Butler has been a five-time All-NBA Team member.
Jimmy Butler has been a five-time NBA All-Defensive Team member.
Jimmy Butler won a gold medal as a member of the 2016 U.S. Olympic team.
Jimmy Butler played one year of college basketball for Tyler Junior College before transferring to Marquette University.
Jimmy Butler was selected with the 30th overall pick in the 2011 NBA draft by the Chicago Bulls.
In 2015, Jimmy Butler was named the NBA Most Improved Player.
After six seasons in Chicago, Jimmy Butler was traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves in June 2017.
Jimmy Butler was again traded in November 2018, this time to the Philadelphia 76ers.
In July 2019, Jimmy Butler signed with the Miami Heat via a sign and trade with the 76ers.
During his first season with the Miami Heat, Jimmy Butler reached the NBA Finals.
In 2021, Jimmy Butler led the league in steals.
In 2023, Jimmy Butler led the eighth-seeded Miami Heat to their second NBA Finals in four years.
Jimmy Butler's father abandoned the family when he was an infant.
By the time Jimmy Butler was 13 years old and living in Tomball, his mother kicked him out of the house.
Jimmy Butler's mother told him, "I don't like the look of you. You gotta go."
Despite all this, Jimmy Butler maintains a close relationship with his parents.
In a summer basketball league before his senior year at Tomball High School, Jimmy Butler was noticed by Jordan Leslie and challenged to a three-point shooting contest.
The two immediately became friends, and Butler began staying at Leslie's house.
Butler's friend's mother and stepfather were initially reluctant but took him in within a few months.
As a junior at Tomball High, Jimmy Butler averaged 10 points per game.
As a senior and team captain in the 2006–07 season, Jimmy Butler averaged 19.9 points and 8.7 rebounds per game and was voted his team's most valuable player.
Jimmy Butler was not heavily recruited coming out of high school and chose to attend Tyler Junior College in Tyler, Texas.
After his freshman season at Tyler Junior College, where he had averaged 18.1 points, Jimmy Butler drew interest from Division I programs.
Considered a two-star recruit by 247Sports.com, Jimmy Butler was listed as the No. 127 junior college prospect in 2008.
Butler accepted an athletic scholarship to attend Marquette, where he played as a sophomore in the 2008–09 season and averaged 5.6 points and 3.9 rebounds per game.
In the 2009–10 campaign, Butler moved into the starting lineup as a junior and averaged 14.7 points and 6.4 rebounds per game, earning All-Big East Honorable Mention honors.
His season was highlighted by two game-winning shots versus UConn and St. John's.
As a senior in 2010–11, Jimmy Butler averaged 15.7 points per game and earned an All-Big East Honorable Mention for the second straight year.
Jimmy Butler was selected with the 30th overall pick in the 2011 NBA draft by the Chicago Bulls.
In his rookie year, Jimmy Butler played 42 games during the lockout-shortened 2011–12 season.
The following season, Jimmy Butler played all 82 games for the Bulls.
After playing limited minutes to begin the 2012–13 season, Jimmy Butler saw significant minutes over the second half of the season, including starting all 12 playoff games.
In an April 9, 2013, regular season game, Jimmy Butler scored a then career-high 28 points in a 101–98 loss against the Toronto Raptors.
Two days later, he recorded his first NBA double-double game with 22 points and a then career-high 14 rebounds against the New York Knicks.
The 2013–14 season saw Jimmy Butler miss 15 games due to injury, limiting him to 67 games.
He averaged a career-high 38.7 minutes per game in the 2013–14 season, which ranked first in the NBA.
Jimmy Butler scored a season-high 26 points against the Memphis Grizzlies on December 30, 2013.
On January 15, 2014, Jimmy Butler played 60:20 in a triple-overtime game against the Orlando Magic and finished with 21 points, seven rebounds, and six assists.
At the end of the season, Jimmy Butler was named to the NBA All-Defensive Second Team.
On November 25, 2014, Jimmy Butler tied a career high with 32 points in a loss to the Denver Nuggets.
On December 3, 2014, Jimmy Butler was named the Eastern Conference Player of the Month for games played in October/November.
He later set a new career high of 35 points in a 103–97 win over the New York Knicks on December 18, 2014.
On January 29, 2015, Jimmy Butler was named a reserve for the Eastern Conference in the 2015 NBA All-Star Game.
On March 2, 2015, Jimmy Butler was ruled out for three to six weeks with a left elbow injury.
He returned to action on March 23 against the Charlotte Hornets, recording 19 points and 9 rebounds in a 98–86 win.

Jimmy Butler set a playoff career high for the second straight game, scoring 31 points in the Bulls' 91–82 win over the Milwaukee Bucks to take a 2–0 lead in their first-round series on April 20, 2015.
On April 25, Jimmy Butler again set a playoff career high with 33 points, in a Bulls' 92–90 loss to the Bucks, cutting their series lead to 3–2.
They went on to win Game 6 of the series, moving them onto the semi-finals where they lost 4–2 to the Cleveland Cavaliers.
On May 7, Jimmy Butler was named the 2014–15 NBA Most Improved Player and became the first player in franchise history to win the award.
Jimmy Butler re-signed with the Bulls to a five-year, $95 million contract on July 9, 2015. The deal included a player option for the fifth year.
On December 9, Jimmy Butler scored a then career-high 36 points in a loss to the Boston Celtics.
He topped that mark with 43 points on December 18, 2015, in a 147–144 quadruple overtime loss to the Detroit Pistons.

On January 3, 2016, Jimmy Butler broke Michael Jordan's team record for points in a half, scoring 40 of his 42 after the break to lead the Bulls to a 115–113 win over the Toronto Raptors. He also had 10 rebounds and six assists.
On February 5, 2016, Jimmy Butler suffered a left knee strain in a game against the Denver Nuggets and missed nearly four weeks.
He was voted to play in the 2016 NBA All-Star Game but the injury forced him to drop out, and he was subsequently replaced in the East team by teammate Pau Gasol.

Jimmy Butler missed 11 games with the knee injury and returned to action on March 5 against the Houston Rockets. In 34 minutes of action, he recorded 24 points, 11 rebounds, 6 assists, and 1 steal in a 108–100 win, helping the Bulls snap a four-game losing streak.

Jimmy Butler was traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves on June 22, 2017, along with the rights to Justin Patton (the 16th pick in the 2017 NBA draft), for Zach LaVine, Kris Dunn and the rights to Lauri Markkanen (the seventh pick in the 2017 NBA draft).
In his debut for the Timberwolves on October 18, 2017, Jimmy Butler scored 12 points in a 107–99 loss to the San Antonio Spurs.
On December 3, 2017, Jimmy Butler scored 20 of his 33 points in the fourth quarter of the Timberwolves' 112–106 win over Los Angeles Clippers.
On December 12, 2017, Jimmy Butler scored 38 points in a 118–112 overtime loss to the Philadelphia 76ers.
On December 18, 2017, Jimmy Butler had a 37-point effort in a 108–107 win over the Portland Trail Blazers.
On December 27, 2017, Jimmy Butler scored 12 of Minnesota's 14 points in overtime and finished with a season-high 39 to lift the Timberwolves to a 128–125 victory over the Denver Nuggets.
Jimmy Butler was named a Western Conference All-Star reserve on January 23, 2017.

On February 9, 2017, in his return to Chicago, Jimmy Butler scored 38 points in a 114–113 loss to the Bulls. He chose not to play in the All-Star Game, prioritizing the stretch run of the season and thought the rest would benefit him.

On February 23, 2017, Jimmy Butler left the game late in the third quarter with a right knee injury against the Houston Rockets. Two days later, he underwent meniscus surgery and was ruled out indefinitely.
Jimmy Butler returned to action on April 6, 2017, to score 18 points in a 113–96 win over the Los Angeles Lakers.

In Game 3 of the Timberwolves' first-round playoff series against the Rockets, Jimmy Butler hit four 3-pointers among his 28 points in a 121–105 win. The Timberwolves went on to lose the series in five games.
Shortly before training camp in 2018, Jimmy Butler requested a trade from the Timberwolves, indicating he would not re-sign with the team in the 2019 off-season.

When a trade was not achieved prior to the start of the regular season, Jimmy Butler opted to play for Minnesota in 2018–19. He appeared in 10 of the Timberwolves' first 13 games before being traded in early November.
On November 12, 2018, Jimmy Butler was traded, along with Justin Patton, to the Philadelphia 76ers in exchange for Jerryd Bayless, Robert Covington, Dario Šarić and a 2022 second-round draft pick.
He made his debut for the 76ers two days later, scoring 14 points in a 111–106 loss to the Orlando Magic.
On November 25, 2018, Jimmy Butler recorded 34 points and 12 rebounds and made a 3-pointer with 2.3 seconds remaining to give the 76ers a 127–125 victory over the Brooklyn Nets.
On December 5, 2018, Jimmy Butler scored a season-high 38 points in a 113–102 loss to the Toronto Raptors.
Two days later, he had a second straight 38-point game in a 117–111 win over the Detroit Pistons.
On January 29, 2019, Jimmy Butler was shifted to point guard and had 20 points and six assists in a 121–105 win over the Los Angeles Lakers.

In Game 1 of the 76ers' first-round playoff series against the Nets, Jimmy Butler scored a game-high 36 points in a 111–102 loss. In Game 2 of the second round, he had 30 points and 11 rebounds to help the 76ers tie the series at 1–1 with a 94–89 win.
In Game 6, Jimmy Butler scored 25 points in a 112–101 win, helping the 76ers force a Game 7. In Game 7, he made a layup with 4.2 seconds in the fourth quarter to tie the score at 90-90.
On July 6, 2019, Jimmy Butler signed with the Miami Heat via a sign and trade with the 76ers in a four-team trade.
On December 9, 2019, Jimmy Butler was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week after he averaged 27.5 points, 9.0 rebounds, and 8.5 assists per game.
On December 10, 2019, Jimmy Butler recorded a career-high 18 rebounds, along with 20 points and 11 assists in a 135–121 overtime win against the Atlanta Hawks.
On January 30, 2020, Jimmy Butler was named to his fifth NBA All-Star Game.
On February 3, 2020, Jimmy Butler scored a season-high 38 points on 14-of-20 shooting from the field as the Heat beat his former team, the Philadelphia 76ers, 137–106.

On August 31, 2020, in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals, Jimmy Butler scored a then playoff career-high 40 points on 13-of-20 shooting from the field in a 115–104 win over the first-seeded Milwaukee Bucks.
On September 8, 2020, the Miami Heat advanced to the next round after defeating the Milwaukee Bucks in Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
The Miami Heat reached the NBA Finals after defeating the Boston Celtics in the Eastern Conference Finals in six games, earning Jimmy Butler his first finals appearance.

In Game 3 of the NBA Finals, Jimmy Butler finished with 40 points, 11 rebounds, and 13 assists and became the third player in finals history to record a 40+ point triple-double, joining LeBron James (then with Cleveland) in 2015 and Jerry West with the Los Angeles Lakers in 1969.
Jimmy Butler also became the first player to have more points, rebounds, and assists in a finals game than James, who finished with 25 points, 10 rebounds, and eight assists.

In Game 5 of the NBA Finals, Jimmy Butler had 35 points, 12 rebounds, 11 assists, and 5 steals to become the first player to register 35+ points, 10+ rebounds, 10+ assists, and 5+ steals in a finals game.

He became the second player with multiple 30-point triple-doubles in the same finals series, joining James in 2015. He also became the sixth player with multiple triple-doubles in a finals series along with James, Magic Johnson, Larry Bird, Wilt Chamberlain, and Draymond Green.
The Miami Heat came up short against the Los Angeles Lakers in six games.

Jimmy Butler became only the second player in a finals series to lead his team in points, rebounds, assists, steals, and blocks, joining James in 2016. He finished the finals averaging 26.2 points, 8.3 rebounds, 9.8 assists, 2.2 steals, and 0.8 blocks per game.
On February 11, 2021, Jimmy Butler recorded his 10th career triple-double with 27 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in the Heat's 101–94 win over the Houston Rockets.

On February 18, 2021, Jimmy Butler logged his 13th career triple-double with 13 points, 10 rebounds, and 13 assists in a 118–110 win over the Sacramento Kings, becoming the first player in franchise history with three consecutive triple-doubles.
Together with teammate Bam Adebayo who posted 16 points, 12 rebounds, and 10 assists, they became the first pair in league history to register triple-doubles in the same game more than once.
Jimmy Butler finished the regular season leading the league in steals with 2.1 steals per game.
In the playoffs, the Miami Heat were eliminated in a four-game sweep by the Milwaukee Bucks who would go on to win the NBA Finals.

On November 10, 2022, Jimmy Butler scored a season-high 35 points, along with 10 rebounds and eight assists in an 117–112 overtime win over the Charlotte Hornets. He scored eight consecutive Heat points at the end of regulation just to get them into the extra session.

He returned to the lineup after missing the previous seven games with a sore right knee on December 2, 2022, and had a season-high 15 rebounds and 25 points in an 120–116 overtime win over the Boston Celtics.

On January 10, 2023, Jimmy Butler tied his season-high with 35 points, along with seven rebounds, four assists, four steals, and three blocks in an 112–111 win over the Oklahoma City Thunder. He led the way going 23-of-23 from the free throw line, tying Dominique Wilkins for the second-most made free throws without a miss in NBA history.
The Miami Heat set an NBA record by making all 40 of their free throws, the last of those coming on Butler's three-point play with 12.9 seconds left in the game.
On February 10, 2023, Jimmy Butler made a game-winning alley-oop dunk in a 97–95 win over the Houston Rockets.

On March 11, 2023, Jimmy Butler scored a season-high 38 points, including 15 in the final six minutes of the fourth quarter when Miami overcame a 15-point deficit. His three-pointer at the buzzer of regulation sent the game to overtime, which the Heat lost 126–114 against the Orlando Magic.
